name: Gardenia's Torterra vs Mr. Mime, Torterra's last Pokemon
notes: Damage answers are hand-supplied from the HZLA calc's damage panel, since the damage calculator port (calc/) does not exist yet.
Torterra's party_remaining = 0 and Mr. Mime's party_remaining = 5 per the user: 'all of torterra's teammates are dead, and my entire team is alive' (Mr. Mime's box shows a 6-mon team, all alive).

Turn number is not recorded (Field.turn left at its default of 1) because it provably cannot matter: none of Torterra's four moves (Roar, Bulldoze, Rock Climb, Seed Bomb) appear in the Setup First Turn effect table, so that flag contributes exactly 0 to every action regardless of turn.

mr_mime.turns_active: the screenshot does not show how long Mr. Mime has been out. Roar/Whirlwind's Expert block branches on 'target has been in battle for more than 3 turns', so this is a real fact affecting the score, not a free assumption -- the user confirmed <=3 turns (a recent switch-in), set here as 3.

Effectiveness: Torterra's four moves are Normal (Roar), Ground (Bulldoze), Rock (Rock Climb) and Grass (Seed Bomb), all neutral (1x) against Mr. Mime's pure Psychic typing -- no super-effective option exists, so has_super_effective_move is false.

best_damaging_move: Bulldoze/Rock Climb/Seed Bomb are all plain damaging effects (none in sNoDamageCalcMoveEffects), so all three enter the AI's comparable-damage table; Seed Bomb's 43.9-52.4% clearly beats Bulldoze's 32.9-40.2% and Rock Climb's 32.9-39%, so it is the AI's highest-damage move. Roar (0 power) never enters the comparison at all.
None of the three damaging moves can KO from Mr. Mime's full HP (all max rolls stay under 53%).

Bulldoze gets NO Expert speed-lowering bonus despite Torterra being slower and Bulldoze lowering Speed in battle. Vanilla intuition says otherwise (Icy Wind/Rock Tomb/Mud Shot: slower -> 72.7% chance of +2), and those three moves' scraped pages all carry that block -- but Bulldoze's page says '(No applicable AI procedures)', and the mechanism checks out: Expert dispatches by effect index (decomp: BATTLE_EFFECT_LOWER_SPEED_HIT -> Expert_SpeedDownOnHit), and Kaizo's Bulldoze kept Magnitude's effect index for AI purposes (bparkpk's own testing note: 'Bulldoze uses Magnitude calculations for scoring purposes'), which has no Expert handler. The AI is blind to Bulldoze's speed drop. Counterfactual if it did route: Bulldoze {99 or 101} would win 186/256 = 72.7% and this case would flip -- high-stakes fact, good save-state test candidate.
